services.title: Employee Retention Credit
services.summary: The COVID-era credit and whether you qualify.
services.text: The Employee Retention Tax Credit was designed to help employers whose operations were suspended by a government order due to COVID-19, or who had a significant decline in gross receipts.
services.lead: Employee Retention Tax Credit (ERC) was designed to help employers whose operations were suspended, either partially or fully, by a government order due to COVID-19, OR had a significant decline in gross receipts, OR began carrying on business after February 15, 2020.

covers.title: 2020 credit
covers.text: ERC provides up to $5,000 per employee, per year for 2020.

covers.title: 2021 credit
covers.text: ERC provides up to $7,000 per employee, per quarter for the first three quarters of 2021.

covers.title: Eligibility
covers.text: Whether your business is a stand-alone business or part of a group, a member firm can help you determine your eligibility for the ERC.

about.title: A network of boutique CPA and advisory firms with varying specialties.
text: Accounting-in-a-Box offers a hub for an array of accounting and consulting services that are traditionally only available together at national or multi-national firms, while keeping the agility, responsiveness and personalized services that are often seen at smaller firms.

Services that our members render include audit, tax, R&D tax credits, tax incentives, bookkeeping, business valuation, part-time CFO, M&A advisory and more. With a focus on small and midsize businesses and business owners, our professionals know firsthand the challenges that small and midsize businesses face daily, and have served as their trusted partners for a number of years. We are known for client-focused and reasonable fees.

Browse the provider directory and filter by your location, industry, revenue size and service specialty. If the service you need is not listed, send us an email and we will find a service provider for you. Come back to see our new members as well, because we are growing.

faqs.q: Can I extend the deadline to file my individual income tax return without filing a form?
faqs.a: Yes. You can extend the deadline to file your individual income tax return to October 15 simply by making a tax payment on the IRS website at irs.gov/payments. Select Form 1040 and then choose Extension as the reason for payment.

faqs.q: How long does the IRS have to audit a return?
faqs.a: The IRS generally has three years from the due date of the return or the date it was filed, whichever is later, to audit and adjust it. That stretches to six years if a person fails to report over 25% of gross income.

faqs.q: How long should I keep tax returns and supporting documents?
faqs.a: Keep them at least as long as the IRS has to audit the return, which is generally three years from the later of the due date or the filing date, and six years where over 25% of gross income went unreported.

faqs.q: How often should a business valuation be updated?
faqs.a: Any private company that issues equity-based compensation to U.S. employees and advisors has to comply with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code, which requires that stock options and other equity incentives are not priced below fair market value when issued.

faqs.q: What is an earn-out when selling a business?
faqs.a: An earn-out is a contingent portion of the purchase price of an acquisition, determined after closing based on the target company's performance against contractually defined criteria or benchmarks. Part of the price is paid at closing and the rest follows.

faqs.q: Does the IRS pay interest on refunds?
faqs.a: Normally the IRS is required to pay interest on a refund if the refund is issued after a statutory period. By law the interest rate on both overpayment and underpayment of tax is adjusted quarterly.

faqs.q: What if the service I need is not in the provider directory?
faqs.a: Send an email or fill out the request form with your company name and website, and we will find a service provider for you. Financial planning and property tax enquiries are routed the same way.

facts.heading: How membership works
facts.text: Accounting and advisory services are rendered via Accounting-in-a-Box's member firms, and membership includes both CPA firms and non-CPA firms. In order to use the mark, a firm must be a current member, and members are required to maintain certain standards. Only the firms listed on accountinginabox.com are current members, and member firms are independent from each other.
